author: Claude Opus 5.5 (engineering lead, cand-d author)
summary: Family B, cand-d v7 (Q99). Three radially carried balls at 120 degrees meet short straight tangential cheeks and axially opposed pads and shutters. No central stud, V clamp or Hirth teeth. A mechanically captured head servo moves three transverse keepers; a separately timed barrel track moves the rear stops outward. The enclosed two-segment body and internal hinge provide articulation. This is an exploratory candidate, not an accepted mechanism.

assembly_access.statement: Build each short metal cartridge outside the shell. Fit captive rear-stop spider and guide rods, cam drum and two radial lands, keeper pickups and runners, then front guides. Gauge the three travel paths individually through a complete forward and reverse rotation. Secure the gauged 28T input hub with the axial rocker screw before fitting the cartridge, engage the floating torque tongues through the front opening, secure the two projecting ears from outside into captive metal nuts. Install each radial ball carrier and threaded tail plate before the tail controller. Retain v6's cassette-to-floor and side-brace screws, metal nut ledges, insulated harness and removable lids. The swept model is a paper screen; tool access at the interior runners, drive overload and recovery remain unverified.

coupler_sites.mount: Two staggered M1.6 flush screws, captive 304 nuts, fixed front steel plate; pitch datum x37.25, common axis y+0.60 z-4.60 mm.
Tail station flange at x-11.60, fastened from inside tail into blind metal threads. Same centreline as head; three 120-degree sites.

retention.mechanism: Inside the closed travel dwell, parallel rear pads and transverse keeper faces enclose three axial poles. Each opposing pair of short cheeks bounds the tangential poles of its own sphere. Axials carry pull/push and pitch/yaw; tangentials carry shear and twist, with no required adjacent reaction at a smaller lever arm. Rigid dwell and stops are the proposed powered-off mechanism, not motor holding torque. A six-coordinate bound holds for flat smooth pole contacts with positive opposite-side gaps. Neither zero backlash nor fully loaded transit follows from this bound. The current closure has no independent finite-preload device to absorb axial tolerances as Q85 requires.

release.means: The head alone withdraws each keeper, then drives a common stripper against the balls toward the mouths. These motions are mechanically sequenced, not a command to unlink. The planar cam takes up drag at the ball and guide surfaces; the barrel cam must also overcome an eccentrically loaded rear-pad guide. Normal-edge forces, rated push on the last loaded pad and obstruction recovery are not bounded over all release states. No release under worst load is claimed.

alignment.description: Three straight tangential cheek pairs, rear seating flats, and transverse keeper ends; no alignment magnets.
alignment.justification: The spheres enter short parallel throats under a quasistatic presentation. The cheek normals control transverse position and roll; the rear seats oppose axial overtravel and set pitch and yaw at three separated points. No independent force is supplied for active centring or flattening a mispresented neighbor. A partial or obstructed presentation is not a locked joint. No capture window claimed.

limitations: Gate 1 is exploratory paper feasibility; no real prototype, dynamic solver, R10 or later acceptance result.
Clearance in axial and transverse pairs is real. The design does not meet Q85 axial tolerance take-up by a torque-limited stop; no additional load path or spring is assumed.
The six-reaction bound is conditional on spherical flat-land contact, no seventh contact and bounded friction, location, deformation and normal errors. It is not a release-path certificate.
Servo shaft position and current do not report three blade positions or actual ball seating. No lock indication or automatic recovery is credited.
Gross stock and projected box allocations conservatively charge material; they do not establish every internal 3D clearance or contact sequence.
No inter-unit power, autonomous capture, full five-kin chain articulation, impact survival or fatigue life claimed.
